\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عاشق} \fa{شدن} ('âsheq shodan)}{عاشق شدن ('âsheq shodan)}]{\fa{عاشق} \fa{شدن} ('âsheq shodan) — to fall in love}

\label{lesson:FA-C334-asheq-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for middle age, then the Persian for old age.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عاشق} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{عاشق} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{'âsheq shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to fall in love\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{دانشگاه} \fa{عاشق} \fa{همکلاسی} \fa{اش} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U dar dâneshgâh 'âsheq-e hamkelâsi-ash shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He fell in love with his classmate at university.
\end{quote}

The loved one follows with the ezafe: \emph{'âsheq-e u shod}. Present \emph{'âsheq mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'âsheq} \textquotedblleft{}in love, a lover\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{'āshiq}, \textquotedblleft{}lover\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'âsheq shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{'âsheq shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{'âsheq shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for middle age, then the Persian for old age, then say \emph{'âsheq shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{عاشق} \fa{شدن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To fall in love\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خواستگاری} (khâstegâri)}{خواستگاری (khâstegâri)}]{\fa{خواستگاری} (khâstegâri) — a marriage proposal}

\label{lesson:FA-C334-khastegari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for old age, then the Persian for to fall in love.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خواستگاری}}
\textbf{\fa{خواستگاری}} (\emph{khâstegâri}) — \textquotedblleft{}a marriage proposal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خواستگاری} \fa{در} \fa{خانه} \fa{پدر} \fa{دختر} \fa{انجام} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Khâstegâri dar khâne-ye pedar-e dokhtar anjâm shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The proposal took place at the young woman's family home.
\end{quote}

Traditionally the man's family visits the woman's family to ask for her hand. From \emph{khâstan} \textquotedblleft{}to want, to ask for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâstegâri} is built on \emph{khâste}, from the native verb \emph{khâstan} \textquotedblleft{}to want, to ask for\textquotedblright{}, with the suffixes \emph{-gâr} and \emph{-i}: the asking. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khâstegâri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khâstegâri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khâstegâri}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for old age, then the Persian for to fall in love, then say \emph{khâstegâri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{خواستگاری} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A marriage proposal\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خواستگاری} \fa{کردن} (khâstegâri kardan)}{خواستگاری کردن (khâstegâri kardan)}]{\fa{خواستگاری} \fa{کردن} (khâstegâri kardan) — to propose marriage}

\label{lesson:FA-C334-khastegari-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to fall in love, then the Persian for a marriage proposal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خواستگاری} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خواستگاری} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{khâstegâri kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to propose marriage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{یک} \fa{سال} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{دختر} \fa{خواستگاری} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U yek sâl ba'd az dokhtar khâstegâri kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A year later he proposed to the young woman.
\end{quote}

The person asked takes \emph{az}. Present \emph{khâstegâri mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khâstegâri kardan} joins the native noun \emph{khâstegâri} \textquotedblleft{}a proposal\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{khâstan} \textquotedblleft{}to want\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}, inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khâstegâri kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khâstegâri kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to fall in love, then the Persian for a marriage proposal, then say \emph{khâstegâri kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نامزدی} (nâmzadi)}{نامزدی (nâmzadi)}]{\fa{نامزدی} (nâmzadi) — an engagement}

\label{lesson:FA-C334-namzadi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a marriage proposal, then the Persian for to propose marriage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نامزدی}}
\textbf{\fa{نامزدی}} (\emph{nâmzadi}) — \textquotedblleft{}an engagement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جشن} \fa{نامزدی} \fa{آنها} \fa{در} \fa{تابستان} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jashn-e nâmzadi-ye ânhâ dar tâbestân bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Their engagement party was in the summer.
\end{quote}

From \emph{nâmzad} \textquotedblleft{}fiancé, fiancée\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}name-struck\textquotedblright{}: a name given to someone.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nâmzadi} adds the suffix \emph{-i} to \emph{nâmzad} \textquotedblleft{}fiancé, fiancée\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{nâm} \textquotedblleft{}name\textquotedblright{} and \emph{zad}, the past stem of \emph{zadan} \textquotedblleft{}to strike\textquotedblright{}. All of it is native Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nâmzadi}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a marriage proposal, then the Persian for to propose marriage, then say \emph{nâmzadi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عقد} ('aqd)}{عقد ('aqd)}]{\fa{عقد} ('aqd) — the marriage contract, the wedding ceremony}

\label{lesson:FA-C334-aqd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to propose marriage, then the Persian for an engagement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عقد}}
\textbf{\fa{عقد}} (\emph{'aqd}) — \textquotedblleft{}the marriage contract, the wedding ceremony\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{عقد} \fa{آنها} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{محضر} \fa{کوچک} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{'Aqd-e ânhâ dar yek mahzar-e kuchak bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Their marriage ceremony was at a small registry office.
\end{quote}

The legal and religious signing; \emph{sofre-ye 'aqd} is the spread laid out for it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'aqd} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{'aqd}, \textquotedblleft{}a contract\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word), from a root for tying a knot.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
